$comment: Shared project settings, committed. Personal overrides belong in
settings.local.json, which is gitignored and merges over this file.
No Stop hook here on purpose. A Stop hook that runs the unit suite would be
cheap and useful, but the checks that actually prove this project works --
eval.py and nis2/benchmark.py -- take minutes of local LLM time and would make
every turn unusable. Run those from /loop, which is bounded and asynchronous.
Add a Stop hook once there is a fast check that is worth blocking on.

$comment_pretooluse: Guardrail for the destructive operations specific to this project.
continueOnBlock lets Claude explain and pick another approach rather than

hooks.prompt:
Judge ONLY the literal command given. Do not block on what a command could hypothetically become, and do not infer an unstated target. If the command names an explicit non-main branch, that branch is the target.

Return {"ok": false, "reason": "blocked: <why>"} if it does any of the following; otherwise {"ok": true}.

Irreversible git: any --force or --force-with-lease push; a push whose explicit target is main or master (`git push origin main`, `git push origin HEAD:main`); a bare `git push` with no branch argument; reset --hard, rebase or filter-branch on already-pushed history. A push naming any other branch (`git push origin feat/x`, `git push -u origin my-branch`) is ALLOWED.

Secrets: printing, copying or committing .env or a credential file; echoing a connection string or password unmasked. Reading .env from application code is fine.

MongoDB Atlas: dropping a database, collection or search index; deleting documents; `main.py --rebuild-mongo`. The free tier allows three search indexes and two are in use, so a dropped index may not be recreatable. Read-only checks like `--mongo-status` are ALLOWED.

Baseline data: writing to nis2/ground_truth.json or eval_questions.json. These are the hand-labelled baselines the benchmarks score against, and editing them to make a check pass destroys the only independent signal the project has. Reading them is ALLOWED.

Expensive rebuilds: `main.py --rebuild-index` or `--rebuild-graph`, each minutes of local embedding.

Destructive filesystem: rm -rf outside a build, cache or temp directory.
